question: Do information-theoretic views of end-to-end CNN training justify a greedy layer-wise objective that combines local classification loss with representation entropy, and does that objective provide an accurate, efficient alternative to end-to-end backpropagation for CIFAR and traffic-sign tasks?

key_findings.claim: The proposed Greedy-DIB method does not eliminate cross-entropy loss or backpropagation as the abstract and introduction state; it replaces global end-to-end error propagation with cross-entropy-trained, locally backpropagated blocks.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 5 defines the DIB surrogate as cross-entropy plus beta times representation entropy, Equation 7 repeats the cross-entropy term for every block, Figure 7 draws local red gradient paths, and Section 4.2.2 says the current block and auxiliary classifier are updated while the other blocks are fixed. The accurate distinction is local versus global backpropagation, not training without cross-entropy or gradients.

key_findings.claim: Cross-mutual-information heatmaps suggest that shallow representations become dependent on their final-epoch counterparts earlier than deep representations, but they do not establish layer-wise parameter or loss convergence.
key_findings.evidence: The matrix entry at epoch t is I(z_i^t; z_j^T), where T is the final network, and Figure 3 shows diagonal dependence growing earlier in shallow VGG16 and ResNet18 layers during 1,000-epoch CIFAR-10 runs. Mutual information with a final representation can change through scale, nuisance content, or estimator behavior and is not a convergence criterion for weights, gradients, local loss, or held-out prediction. No seeds, uncertainty, threshold, or replicated heatmaps are reported.

key_findings.claim: The auto-MI/MDS visualization cannot support claims about absolute movement across epochs unless the independently computed two-dimensional embeddings are aligned, and the paper reports no such alignment.
key_findings.evidence: At each epoch the authors construct a new L-by-L normalized-MI distance matrix and project it with multidimensional scaling, then interpret larger coordinate movement in deep layers as slower training. Separate MDS solutions are invariant to translation, rotation, and reflection. The method does not state that all epochs are embedded jointly, initialized identically, or Procrustes-aligned, so apparent trajectory length may include coordinate-system drift.

key_findings.claim: The modified information plane is descriptive evidence for a fitted-and-compressed trajectory under one matrix-based entropy estimator, not proof that end-to-end training obeys a Markov information-bottleneck principle.
key_findings.evidence: The authors plot H(z_l) against I(z_l;y) for selected VGG16 and ResNet18 layers and observe rising then falling H(z_l) while label information rises. The feed-forward deterministic chain is already Markov by architecture, while the plotted trajectory does not test conditional independence, optimality, minimal sufficiency, or a causal information-flow mechanism. Figure 6 provides no replicate runs, estimator sensitivity, or quantitative test.

key_findings.claim: Replacing I(Z;X) by H(Z) is formally delicate for continuous deterministic neural representations, and the matrix-based Renyi functional is a kernel surrogate rather than an automatically interchangeable Shannon entropy.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 2-3 use H(Z|X)=0 to reduce deterministic IB, and the footnote on page 9 makes the same substitution between adjacent layers. For continuous deterministic mappings, ordinary mutual information can be infinite and differential conditional entropy is not generally zero in the discrete-entropy sense. Equations 9-10 instead define eigenvalue functionals of finite Gram matrices with alpha=1.01; the paper does not prove that the Shannon identities used in the derivation hold exactly for those minibatch surrogates.

anchors.section: Appendix A, Equation 10 and estimator settings

key_findings.claim: Greedy-DIB trains each block and an auxiliary head with a local minimal-sufficiency surrogate, then discards intermediate heads at inference.
key_findings.evidence: For each block z_l=f_l(z_{l-1}), an auxiliary classifier predicts y. The local objective is CE(g(z_l);y)+beta H(z_l), with H estimated from the eigenvalues of a trace-normalized RBF Gram matrix. During a block update all other blocks are fixed; Figure 1 says auxiliary classifiers are discarded at test time.

key_findings.claim: The published training algorithm is internally ambiguous about whether blocks are trained to completion successively or all blocks are updated inside each outer minibatch loop.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.2.1 says L blocks are trained in succession and Section 4.2.2 describes updating only layer l while all others are fixed. Algorithm 1 instead places a loop over every j=1,...,L inside a single while loop and writes an update for theta_l rather than theta_j, without defining the stopping criterion or freezing/activation schedule. The implementation section reports epochs per layer but does not resolve whether data and augmentation are replayed separately for each block.

key_findings.claim: On a five-layer CIFAR-10 CNN, Greedy-DIB matches the single reported SGD accuracy and substantially exceeds the four reported local-learning baselines.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 reports test accuracy of 84.66% for Greedy-DIB, 84.63% for end-to-end SGD, 83.27% for Greedy LS, 83.58% for Greedy LE, 61.56% for HSIC bottleneck, and 60.72% for NIK. Beta=0.006 is selected as best from a 0.001-0.01 sweep shown in Figure 8(b), but the selection split, number of runs, seeds, and uncertainty are omitted.

key_findings.claim: Across every VGG and ResNet CIFAR configuration in Table 3, Greedy-DIB beats the reported layer-wise baselines but loses to end-to-end SGD, with the largest gap on CIFAR-100 ResNet18.
key_findings.evidence: For CIFAR-10, SGD versus Greedy-DIB is 90.37 versus 90.22 on VGG11, 92.64 versus 92.21 on VGG16, and 93.02 versus 91.73 on ResNet18. For CIFAR-100 it is 68.64 versus 67.63, 72.93 versus 69.75, and 75.61 versus 72.03, respectively. Thus the claimed performance 'on par with SGD' ranges from a 0.15-point to a 3.58-point deficit and is unsupported by equivalence bounds or uncertainty.

key_findings.claim: The latent-space illustration in Figure 9 is qualitative and under-specified, so it does not independently show that the entropy term creates more separable or minimal representations.
key_findings.evidence: The first row is labeled Greedy-DIB and the second local cross-entropy without DIB for layers 1-5, but the projection method, sample count, class encoding, random seed, quantitative separability metric, and uncertainty are not stated. Visual cluster spacing in an unspecified two-dimensional projection is not evidence of information minimality.

key_findings.claim: The reported traffic-sign results favor Greedy-DIB, but only by small single-run point estimates on curated sign crops rather than a full in-the-wild detection benchmark.
key_findings.evidence: On CTSRD Table 4 reports 98.73% classification accuracy and 89.23% mIoU for Greedy-DIB versus 98.23% and 86.31% for SGD; Greedy LE already reaches 98.68% and 88.56%. On GTSRB Table 5 reports 97.88% accuracy versus 97.38% for SGD and omits mIoU because boxes are absent. Images are resized to 64x64 and signs average about 20% of each image, while no variance, detector precision/recall, AP, false positives on sign-free scenes, or significance is provided.

key_findings.claim: GTSRB does not evaluate the paper's claimed two-head detection contribution because it has no bounding-box labels, and CTSRD evaluation does not establish scene-level traffic-sign detection.
key_findings.evidence: The paper explicitly omits GTSRB mIoU for lack of bounding-box ground truth. It also states that the target occupies a substantial fraction of the image in both datasets. The challenging Tsinghua-Tencent 100K regime, where signs occupy less than 1% of wild images, is excluded and deferred to future YOLO work. Classification plus box regression on sign-centered images does not test proposal generation, background rejection, or multiple-object detection.

key_findings.claim: The central efficiency motivation is not evaluated and the nominal training schedules are not compute-matched.
key_findings.evidence: The paper reports no peak memory, retained activation memory, wall time, FLOPs, throughput, energy, or device. The five-layer model trains each block for 100 epochs and VGG/ResNet blocks for 50 epochs, so VGG16 entails 13 separately trained blocks and auxiliary classifiers. The comparable end-to-end schedule and total examples or optimizer steps are not stated, while every batch also requires a B-by-B Gram matrix and eigendecomposition for the entropy term.

key_findings.claim: Several empirical choices weaken reproducibility and allow model-selection confounds.
key_findings.evidence: No code or artifact link, seed, number of runs, confidence interval, validation protocol, hardware, stopping rule, or checkpoint selection rule is reported. Beta is swept on the simple CNN and then changed to 0.01 for traffic signs; baseline hyperparameters are said to follow original settings, but no implementation validation is shown. HSIC and NIK are omitted from traffic-sign tables because their results are poor.

key_findings.claim: The conclusion's claims of large-scale data and first real-world superiority over end-to-end backpropagation exceed the tested evidence.
key_findings.evidence: The largest generic benchmark is CIFAR-100, despite prior greedy layer-wise work explicitly scaling to ImageNet. The traffic datasets contain sign-centered images and only CTSRD supplies boxes; the strongest margin over SGD is reported without repeated trials or compute matching. The paper itself acknowledges that true tiny-sign wild imagery requires a different detector architecture and remains future work.

method.core_idea: Use matrix-based information measurements to motivate training a CNN one block at a time with a local deterministic-information-bottleneck surrogate: classification cross-entropy plus an entropy penalty on the block representation.
method.mechanism: The analysis first compares every layer at epoch t with every final-epoch layer through a cross-MI matrix, embeds within-epoch normalized-MI distances with MDS, and plots representation entropy against label mutual information. Greedy-DIB partitions VGG, ResNet, or a simple CNN into gradient-isolated blocks. For block l, a temporary auxiliary classifier predicts the label and the block plus head are optimized by CE(g(z_l);y)+beta H_alpha(z_l), while other blocks are fixed. H_alpha is computed from eigenvalues of a trace-normalized RBF Gram matrix over the minibatch, with alpha=1.01 and bandwidth set from mean tenth-neighbor distances. Traffic-sign blocks add an L1 bounding-box head. Intermediate heads are discarded after their blocks have been trained.
assumptions: Matrix-based Renyi entropy and mutual-information functionals preserve the Shannon-information interpretations used to motivate the objective.
For continuous deterministic neural mappings, replacing I(Z;X) with H(Z) yields a well-defined and useful deterministic-bottleneck objective.
High cross-MI with a final-epoch representation means a layer has converged in the optimization-relevant sense.
MDS coordinates from different training epochs are comparable without a reported joint embedding or alignment step.
The entropy trajectory and feed-forward architecture demonstrate an information-bottleneck principle rather than an estimator- or visualization-specific pattern.
A local auxiliary classifier can force each block to retain information needed by later blocks without causing greedy information loss.
Penalizing minibatch kernel entropy removes nuisance information rather than class-relevant within-class variation.
The chosen RBF bandwidth, alpha, beta, batch size, and auxiliary-head capacity transfer across layers, architectures, and datasets.
Sequential block epochs are comparable in optimization opportunity and total compute to the unstated end-to-end training budget.
Single reported accuracies and mIoU values reflect stable method effects rather than initialization, data-order, tuning, or checkpoint noise.
Bounding-box regression on sign-centered crops represents real-world traffic-sign detection.
Local gradient isolation reduces practical memory and compute despite auxiliary heads and repeated Gram eigendecompositions.

techniques.role: Compares all epoch-t layer representations with all final-epoch representations to visualize claimed shallow-to-deep convergence.
Projects normalized within-network layer-dependence distances into two dimensions at successive epochs.
Plots layer representation entropy against label mutual information to motivate a local compression term.
Optimizes one CNN block and its auxiliary head while holding the remaining blocks fixed.
Balances local supervised cross-entropy against beta-weighted representation entropy.
Estimates entropy from eigenvalues of a trace-normalized minibatch RBF Gram matrix with alpha=1.01.
Sets the Gram-kernel width from the average tenth-nearest-neighbor distance in a minibatch.
Provides each hidden block with a local label-prediction objective and is removed at inference.
Adds an auxiliary L1 bounding-box regressor to the local entropy and classification terms.

evaluations.setting: VGG16 and ResNet18 trained end to end on CIFAR-10 for 1,000 epochs
evaluations.metric: Cross-MI heatmaps, normalized auto-MI/MDS layer trajectories, and modified information-plane trajectories
evaluations.result: The visualizations are interpreted as shallow layers approaching final representations first and individual layers showing fitting followed by entropy compression; no scalar convergence test, repeat-run uncertainty, or estimator sensitivity is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Final-epoch representations for cross-MI and the paper's cited SVCCA observation; no experimental alternative MI estimator or conventional loss/gradient convergence baseline

evaluations.setting: Five-layer, 256-filter CNN on CIFAR-10, trained for 100 epochs per block with batch size 256
evaluations.result: Greedy-DIB 84.66%, end-to-end SGD 84.63%, Greedy LS 83.27%, Greedy LE 83.58%, HSIC bottleneck 61.56%, and NIK 60.72%.
evaluations.baseline: End-to-end SGD plus four local-learning methods

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 with VGG11, VGG16, and ResNet18, each Greedy-DIB block trained for 50 epochs
evaluations.result: Greedy-DIB reaches 90.22%, 92.21%, and 91.73%, respectively, versus end-to-end SGD at 90.37%, 92.64%, and 93.02%; it exceeds every reported layer-wise baseline.
evaluations.baseline: End-to-end SGD, Greedy LS, Greedy LE, HSIC bottleneck, and NIK

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100 with VGG11, VGG16, and ResNet18
evaluations.result: Greedy-DIB reaches 67.63%, 69.75%, and 72.03%, respectively, versus SGD at 68.64%, 72.93%, and 75.61%; deficits are 1.01, 3.18, and 3.58 percentage points despite beating the local baselines.
evaluations.baseline: End-to-end SGD, Greedy LS, Greedy LE, HSIC bottleneck, and NIK

evaluations.setting: CTSRD: 6,164 images in 58 classes, resized to 64 by 64 with an 80/20 split and a five-layer fully convolutional network
evaluations.metric: Classification accuracy and mean intersection over union
evaluations.result: Greedy-DIB reports 98.73% accuracy and 89.23% mIoU, compared with SGD at 98.23% and 86.31%, Greedy LS at 98.62% and 87.45%, and Greedy LE at 98.68% and 88.56%.
evaluations.baseline: End-to-end SGD, Greedy LS, and Greedy LE; HSIC bottleneck and NIK are omitted

evaluations.setting: GTSRB: 39,209 training and 12,630 test images in 43 classes with VGG16
evaluations.result: Greedy-DIB reports 97.88%, compared with SGD at 97.38%, Greedy LS at 97.32%, and Greedy LE at 97.48%; mIoU is unavailable because the dataset has no bounding-box labels.
evaluations.baseline: End-to-end SGD, Greedy LS, and Greedy LE; no valid detection baseline

limitations: The paper repeatedly says layer-wise learning removes cross-entropy and backpropagation, but the proposed method explicitly uses both within every block; only global error propagation is removed.
The statement that backpropagation retains all hidden-layer weights misidentifies the main training-memory issue, which is normally retained activations and optimizer state as well as parameters.
Cross-MI with the final network is an exploratory dependence statistic and is not validated as a measure of layer, parameter, or objective convergence.
Epoch-specific MDS plots are compared without a reported common coordinate system or alignment procedure.
The deterministic information-bottleneck derivation does not address continuous-variable singularities or establish that the matrix-based Renyi surrogate obeys each Shannon identity invoked.
The Markov information-bottleneck conclusion is not independently tested; the Markov property is substantially supplied by feed-forward architecture.
The local-training pseudocode contains an l-versus-j indexing inconsistency and does not specify the stopping or block-freezing schedule unambiguously.
No source code, environment, hardware, seed, number of trials, run variance, confidence interval, or significance test is supplied.
Beta=0.006 is selected as the best point of a CIFAR-10 sweep without identifying a validation-only selection protocol, and beta changes across experiments.
Figure 9's latent representation has no stated projection method, quantitative cluster metric, or repeat-run stability analysis.
Training budgets are not matched: Greedy-DIB trains each of up to 13 blocks for 50 epochs and adds auxiliary networks, while the end-to-end schedule and total compute are unspecified.
The claimed memory and computational benefits are never measured, and the B-by-B eigendecomposition adds cubic-in-batch matrix work in a direct implementation.
Greedy-DIB trails SGD in all six VGG/ResNet CIFAR settings, by as much as 3.58 percentage points, without equivalence testing to support 'on par.'
The largest generic dataset is CIFAR-100, so the paper's description of large-scale data is weak relative to prior ImageNet layer-wise studies.
CTSRD and GTSRB contain cropped or sign-dominated images; they do not measure proposal generation, sign-free false positives, multiple-object recall, AP, or tiny-sign scene detection.
GTSRB has no bounding-box ground truth and therefore cannot validate the two-head detector's regression component.
The more realistic Tsinghua-Tencent 100K task is explicitly deferred because signs occupy less than 1% of an image and would require YOLO-style modeling.
HSIC bottleneck and NIK are omitted from traffic-sign tables after being characterized as poor, and no diagnostic establishes that their implementations are competitive.
No comparison is made to stronger recent local-learning, gradient-reconciliation, decoupled-greedy, or genuinely no-backpropagation systems in the experiments.
The traffic margins over SGD and Greedy LE are small point estimates without uncertainty, compute matching, or predeclared model-selection rules.
failure_modes: An entropy penalty can compress task-relevant fine detail, especially for visually similar traffic-sign subclasses and later blocks that cannot recover discarded information.
A block can overfit its temporary auxiliary classifier and learn features that are locally predictive but poorly suited to downstream composition.
Kernel entropy can be dominated by feature scale, batch composition, or bandwidth, making beta effects unstable across layers and batch sizes.
Repeated eigenvalue decompositions of nearly singular Gram matrices can introduce numerical instability or overwhelm any memory and speed gains from gradient isolation.
Independent block training can multiply exposure to augmented samples and optimizer steps, yielding an apparent accuracy advantage that disappears under equal compute.
Without alignment, MDS coordinate drift can be mistaken for deep-layer learning dynamics and lead to a proxy objective motivated by an artifact.
A representation may have high dependence on its final-epoch counterpart while its classifier loss or decision boundary remains far from converged.
Single-run checkpoint noise can reverse margins of 0.03 to 0.50 percentage points on CIFAR-10 and traffic-sign accuracy.
A crop-level box regressor can score high mIoU while failing to find tiny signs in full scenes, reject backgrounds, or handle multiple signs.
A fixed entropy weight can undercompress early blocks and overcompress late blocks because representation dimensionality and kernel spectra change with depth.
Auxiliary-head capacity can account for differences between local methods, confounding the contribution of the deterministic-bottleneck term.
The absence of end-to-end fine-tuning can lock in an early-block mistake that later blocks cannot correct.
reusable_insights: Distinguish elimination of global backpropagation from elimination of local gradients or cross-entropy; diagrams and equations should use the precise claim.
Validate a representation-based convergence proxy against loss, gradient, parameter, and held-out metrics before using it to motivate a training algorithm.
Align MDS embeddings across time, or embed all epochs jointly, before interpreting coordinate trajectories.
State whether entropy and mutual information are Shannon quantities, differential quantities, or kernel functionals and prove only the identities appropriate to that estimator.
A local entropy regularizer is a simple reusable extension to auxiliary-classifier greedy training, but its value must be isolated with an otherwise identical CE-only ablation.
Report per-block schedules, freeze boundaries, data replay, stopping rules, and precise pseudocode for sequential local learning.
Compare local-learning systems at equal examples processed, optimizer steps, auxiliary-head capacity, wall time, and peak memory.
Use multiple seeds and equivalence or noninferiority bounds before calling a local method comparable to end-to-end training.
For deployment claims, measure the proposed resource advantage directly rather than inferring it from a shorter gradient path.
Separate cropped-object classification and localization from full-scene detection, and report AP, recall, false positives, object scale, and multiple-object performance.
open_questions: Does the shallow-to-deep convergence result persist across seeds, optimizers, learning-rate schedules, datasets, and MI estimators when compared with conventional convergence diagnostics?
How do the MDS trajectories change after joint temporal embedding or Procrustes alignment?
Which information-theoretic properties of Shannon IB are actually retained by the finite-sample matrix-based Renyi functional used here?
Can beta and RBF bandwidth be chosen per layer without using test performance, and how sensitive are results to batch size and feature normalization?
What are peak memory, wall-clock time, FLOPs, energy, and throughput for Greedy-DIB versus checkpointed end-to-end backpropagation and current local-learning competitors?
Does Greedy-DIB remain competitive when every method receives equal training examples, optimizer steps, hyperparameter-search budget, and auxiliary capacity?
What is the mean and variance over preregistered seeds for the small accuracy and mIoU improvements on CTSRD and GTSRB?
Would an end-to-end fine-tuning stage recover the CIFAR-100 gap, and would that erase the claimed training-memory advantage?
Can a lower-complexity entropy estimator retain the reported benefit without a minibatch Gram eigendecomposition?
Does the method improve full-scene AP and small-object recall on Tsinghua-Tencent 100K or another detection dataset with background-only images?
How does Greedy-DIB compare with gradient reconciliation, decoupled greedy learning on ImageNet, and methods that actually avoid both forward and backward propagation?
Which block features are discarded by the entropy penalty, and are errors concentrated among visually similar traffic-sign classes?

competitive_landscape.title: Greedy Layerwise Learning Can Scale to ImageNet
competitive_landscape.difference: Belilovsky et al. already show auxiliary-classifier greedy block training on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet with deep convolutional networks. Greedy-DIB adds a matrix-entropy compression term and traffic-sign case studies, but evaluates generic scale only through CIFAR-100 and therefore does not establish the paper's broad novelty claim that prior local methods are limited to MNIST or simple networks.

competitive_landscape.title: Training Neural Networks with Local Error Signals
competitive_landscape.difference: Nokland and Eidnes train deep networks through local auxiliary losses without global backpropagation and supply the Greedy LE baseline used in this paper. Greedy-DIB's incremental element is entropy regularization of each representation; the traffic result is only 0.05 accuracy and 0.67 mIoU above Greedy LE on CTSRD and 0.40 accuracy above it on GTSRB, without uncertainty.

competitive_landscape.title: The HSIC Bottleneck: Deep Learning without Back-Propagation
competitive_landscape.difference: The HSIC Bottleneck already supplies layer-local information-theoretic objectives without auxiliary classifiers or ordinary error backpropagation. Greedy-DIB replaces normalized HSIC with a deterministic-IB entropy-plus-CE surrogate and performs much better in the authors' implementation, but it reintroduces auxiliary heads, local CE, and local backpropagation and provides no compute-matched reproduction audit.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Deterministic Information Bottleneck with Matrix-based Entropy Functional
competitive_landscape.difference: Yu et al. already combine deterministic information bottleneck with the matrix-based entropy functional in deep networks. The present paper's principal methodological change is to deploy that objective greedily per CNN block with temporary classifiers, rather than originate either DIB or the eigenvalue entropy estimator.

competitive_landscape.title: End-to-End Training Induces Information Bottleneck through Layer-Role Differentiation: A Comparative Analysis with Layer-wise Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Sakamoto and Sato directly compare end-to-end and layer-wise training through information bottleneck and layer-role differentiation, including saturation of usable label information. Greedy-DIB adds cross-MI/MDS visualizations and turns its descriptive observations into a local entropy objective, but does not rigorously identify that the observations require or validate that objective.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Layer-wise Networks Have Closed-Form Weights
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. provide the NIK baseline and a layer-wise system with closed-form kernel-alignment weights, avoiding iterative backpropagation for the local objective. Greedy-DIB is substantially more accurate in the paper's reported CNN tables but requires SGD, cross-entropy, auxiliary heads, and Gram eigendecompositions; the tradeoff is not evaluated in time or memory.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Interpretable Deep Local Learning with Successive Gradient Reconciliation
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. reconcile successive local gradients, report competitive CNN and Transformer performance including ImageNet, and measure more than 40% training-memory savings. This is a closer current test of Greedy-DIB's accuracy-and-efficiency claims than the older baselines, yet Greedy-DIB neither compares against it nor measures the resource outcome at the center of its motivation.

competitive_landscape.title: NoProp: Training Neural Networks without Back-propagation or Forward-propagation
competitive_landscape.difference: NoProp is a current official-proceedings competitor that explicitly avoids both back-propagation and forward-propagation in its training formulation. It sharpens the terminology problem in Greedy-DIB: Greedy-DIB still performs local forward computation, CE optimization, and backpropagation, so its defensible claim is gradient isolation rather than training without backpropagation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim that end-to-end CNNs inherently converge layer by layer under a Markov information-bottleneck principle, that this observation motivates a novel Greedy-DIB local objective, and that the method is the first real-world case in which greedy layer-wise training beats end-to-end backpropagation.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Pages 7-12 present cross-MI, MDS, and information-plane visualizations; pages 13-14 define the per-block entropy-plus-cross-entropy objective; Tables 2-5 report CIFAR and traffic-sign point estimates; pages 18-19 explicitly exclude the more demanding tiny-sign wild-scene setting.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is a straightforward but potentially useful composition: apply an existing matrix-based deterministic-information-bottleneck surrogate as the local objective in an existing auxiliary-head greedy CNN template, then extend it with a local bounding-box head. The convergence interpretation is exploratory, the DIB and matrix entropy are prior work, greedy auxiliary training already scales to ImageNet, and stronger current local methods report scale and memory directly. Greedy-DIB beats the paper's selected local baselines but loses to SGD in all six deep-CIFAR cells; its traffic advantages are small, unreplicated crop-level estimates. It therefore does not establish removal of cross-entropy/backpropagation, compute or memory superiority, equivalence to SGD, or first real-world detection superiority.
